704754.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ennéwə, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁néwn̥. Cognates include Old Armenian ինն (inn), Sanskrit नव (náva), Latin novem, and Old English nigon (English nine).

704701.t: From ἐν (en, “in”) + δύω (dúō, “to enter”). Compare Latin induo.

704792.t: Neuter substantive of *ἔντερος (*énteros, “inside”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁énteros, from *h₁én (whence also ἐν (en, “in”)) + *-teros (whence also -τερος (-teros, “comparative suffix”)).

704713.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₁néwn̥dḱomt, from *h₁néwn̥ (whence also ἐννέα (ennéa, “nine”)) + *déḱm̥t (whence also δέκα (déka, “ten”). Cognate with Latin nōnāgintā, Old Armenian իննսուն (innsun).

704736.t: From ἔνθους (énthous), later contracted form of ἔνθεος (éntheos, “possessed by a god”), + -ιάζω (-iázō, denominative verb suffix), influenced by οὐσία (ousía, “essence”).

704745.t: According to Beekes, the etymology is unknown, and he criticizes some of the proposals to date, including Meillet's that the first part is ἔνος (énos, “year”), as in δίενος (díenos, “two years old”), and the second one is from ἰαύω (iaúō).

704709.t: Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀁𐀚𐀏 (e-ne-ka); otherwise unknown. Formerly thought a composite of ἕν (hén) and *ϝέκα (*wéka) (see: ἑκών (hekṓn)).

704718.t: From ἐνεργός (energós, “active, effective”) + -έω (-éō, denominative verbal suffix).

704731.t: From ἐν- (en-, “there”) + -θα (-thă, “towards”). Cognate with Tocharian B entwe (“then; thereupon”).

704732.t: From ἔνθα (énthă, “there; where”) + -δε (-de, “here”, denoting motion towards the topic or speaker).

704793.t: From ἐν- (en-, “there”) + τοῦ (toû, “(medial)”) + -θεν (-then, “from”). For another modification to τοῦ (toû), see οὗτος (hoûtos).

704776.t: From ἐν (en, “in possession of”) + ὅπλον (hóplon, “implements of war”) + -ος (-os, adjectival suffix).

704762.t: From ἐν- (en-, “in-”) + νοέω (noéō, “to perceive, think, deem”).

704794.t: Nominal formation in -σις (-sis) from ἐντυγχάνω (entunkhánō, “to meet with”).
